prompt: The query in the editor has one mistake. Fix it so that it answers this question: for each promotion that started in 2025 (start_date from 1 January to 31 December 2025), how many units were sold on promotion and how many units did its products sell in the baseline? A sales line is on a promotion when it carries that promotion's ID in order_lines.promo_id, whatever its date; where two promotions overlap on a product, a line carries only the deeper one, so it counts once. The baseline ends the day before the promotion's start_date and has as many days as the promotion ran, start_date and end_date both counted; it holds every sales line of the promotion's products in those days, whatever promotion the line carries. Days are sales.order_date, the UTC day of the order. A period with no sale shows 0. Return three columns, in this order: promo_id, promo_units and baseline_units. Return one row for each such promotion. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, check the length of the baseline window against the length of each promotion.
A 7-day promotion needs a 7-day baseline; work the length out from end_date and start_date, both days counted.
starter_sql:
WITH promo AS (
  -- one row per promotion that started in 2025
  SELECT promo_id, start_date, CAST(end_date - start_date + 1 AS INTEGER) AS days
  FROM promotions
  WHERE start_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-31'
), during AS (
  -- one row per promotion that started in 2025
  SELECT p.promo_id, SUM(ol.quantity) AS units
  FROM promo p
  JOIN order_lines ol ON ol.promo_id = p.promo_id
  GROUP BY p.promo_id
), baseline AS (
  -- one row per promotion with a baseline sale
  SELECT p.promo_id, SUM(s.units) AS units
  FROM promo p
  JOIN promotion_products pp ON pp.promo_id = p.promo_id
  JOIN sales s ON s.product_id = pp.product_id
    AND s.order_date BETWEEN p.start_date - 14 AND p.start_date - 1
  GROUP BY p.promo_id
)
SELECT p.promo_id, COALESCE(d.units, 0) AS promo_units, COALESCE(b.units, 0) AS baseline_units
FROM promo p
LEFT JOIN during d ON d.promo_id = p.promo_id
LEFT JOIN baseline b ON b.promo_id = p.promo_id
why_this_works: A baseline of the promotion's own length makes the two totals comparable, whatever each promotion's duration.
